import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first column which is an index
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length1_98/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length1_98/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Perform the join on Source0.right_index == Source1.index (which is the implicit index after reading)
# But since source1 has no index_col=0, its index is default 0..n-1, and source0.right_index matches that index.
# So join source0 and source1 on source0.right_index == source1.index
# source1 has only column '0', source0 has columns ['right_index', '0']

# Reset index of source1 to have 'right_index' as index for join
# Actually, source1 index is 0..499, source0.right_index is 0..999, so join on source0.right_index == source1.index
# We can do left join source0 with source1 on source0.right_index == source1.index

# Join source0 and source1 on source0.right_index == source1.index
joined = source0.merge(source1, left_on='right_index', right_index=True, suffixes=('_x', '_y'))

# Select columns as per target schema ['0_x', '0_y'] and convert to float
target = joined[['0_x', '0_y']].astype(float)

# Write the result to the specified path without the index
target.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_98/target_multisource.csv", index=False)
